newsitem.title: UK: UK's Beckett names competitiveness advisory group.
newsitem.headline: UK's Beckett names competitiveness advisory group.

text.p: Trade Secretary Margaret Beckett on Wednesday named a 19-strong advisory group on competitiveness to develop proposals in partnership with the government aimed at boosting Britain's long-term economic performance.
Beckett announced the panel at a summit in London with 150 business leaders at which said she wanted to steer a course between government direction of the economy and unbridled market forces.

"Both approaches are founded on dogma. Both have been discredited when they have been tried in practice. Our task is to identify a third way -- a way in which both the government and the business community have clearly identified and agreed roles and responsibilities.
"A way in which the dynamics of market forces are used -- not surrendered to, not opposed, but used -- to deliver the results we want," she said.
Beckett said the stock of capital available to each worker in Britain was the lowest of any Group of Seven industrial country as a result of decades of underinvestment.
Labour productivity was 20-30 percent lower than its main competitors, and as a percentage of GDP Britain ranked fifth in the G7 on investment in research and development.
To help improve the picture, Beckett said her department would provide 10 million stg towards research projects that bring together business and Britain's science base.
She said bids would be invited on September 1 with successful projects getting under way next year.
The membership of Beckett's advisory panel is drawn from small companies as well as big multinationals including Glaxo Wellcome Plc, Guinness Plc and British Petroleum Plc.

In a break with the practice of the previous Conservative government, union leaders John Monks and John Edmunds will join business leaders including Adair Turner, the director general of the Confederation of British Industry, on the panel.
"It seems to me to be a proper ambition for the Department of Trade and Industry and this government to put competitiveness through partnership at the centre of our work," she said.
